text.p: Risky repairs on the crippled Mir space station, due to have been carried out at the end of this week, have been postponed, Interfax news agency quoted mission director Viktor Blagov as saying on Tuesday.

It gave no other details. An official at Mission Control outside Moscow told Reuters he could neither confirm nor deny the report. Earlier, a training session was postponed to give the crew, whose commander has fallen ill, more time to rest.

"The sortie of the Russian cosmonauts into the Spektr module to repair the electrical system of the Russian orbital complex, planned for the night of July 19, is postponed to a later date," Interfax said, quoting Blagov.
Earlier, Mission Control put off Tuesday's rehearsal of the repairs saying it wanted to give the crew, whose commander has been taken ill, more time to rest before the risky and complex task.
The work is intended to restore power which was lost last month after Mir's worst accident in its 11 years in space.
A special committee of doctors was to meet during the day to discuss the health of Mir commander Vasily Tsibliyev. He told Mission Control on Monday he had developed cardiovascular problems.
